## Errors

Errors always use the cano
nical body `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;\

n`details` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invali
d, revoked, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant; distinct from a bad key
|\n| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authCha
llenge` carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine; see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key
is valid but not allowed to do this, or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a diff
erent MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters
|\n| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts
this write, such as a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and
retry |\n| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too m
any requests; see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to the target MCP server |\n| `T
IMEOUT` | 504 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |\n| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our s

ide |

New error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says ot

herwise.

### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API
never starts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:\n\n* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers\
n `403 AUTH_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requ
iredScope`, and\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authent
icate\"]`** (the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\n unchanged with an additive `au

thChallenge` field (`source:
 "tool_result_meta"`). A field the server already set under that name is never
 overwritten.
\
n`AUTH_REQUIRED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for th
at server yourself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See\n[Mid-session sign-in](https

://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, wit

h bursts up to **10**.
Exceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"the

me":"css-variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key ra

to be tuned during the preview.

Other `429`s, the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below, ca
rry `Retry-After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\
nrather than a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\nyour backoff, so **never** block waiting for a heade

r that may not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented (request and response schemas, examples,
and an interac

tive playground) under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog**: discover the IDs everything else takes:

| Endpoint | What

it does |
| - | - |
| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |
| `GET /organizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to
, where `organizationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Project
s the key can access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\
n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and
server info, recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revi
sionNumber}` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too la
rge to store, so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff`
| What changed since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and server info changes with both v
alues. A field listed in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on that side, so a change to it is unknown |\n|
`GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run summaries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{proje
ctId}/clients` | List clients, or create one from a template or full config |\n| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/cli
ents/{client}` | Read, edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a client **name or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/c
lients/{client}/servers` | Replace the client's server attachments (a replacement; omitted servers are detached) |\n| `POST /proje
cts/{projectId}/clients/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config into a new client |\n| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat se

ssions (`?projectId=&status=&limit=&before=`) |

**Project environments**: the named execution bundles (one host, optionally a
standalone server group) that eval suites and goals run against. Reads need\nproject membership. Archiving needs project admin and

is revisioned: pass the
`revision` you last read back as `expectedRevision`, and a stale value returns
`CONFLICT` (409).

| E
ndpoint | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments` | List environments (`?includeArchived=true` to in
clude archived ones) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environment |\n| `GET /projects/{pro
jectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` | Preview the host config and closed server set this environment resolves to right n
ow |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it. The environment is kept, and its name is f

reed for a new one |

| Endpoint | What

it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../validate` | Connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot |
| `POST .../doctor` | Ful
l health workflow: probe → connect → initialize → capabilities |\n| `POST .../check-oauth` | Does this server require an OAuth gra
nt? |\n| `POST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execute a tool; returns the MCP `CallToolResult`
plus additive `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges)) |
\n| `POST .../prompts` | List the server's prompts |\n| `POST .../prompts/get` | Render a prompt; returns the MCP `GetPromptResult

` verbatim |
| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |
| `POST .../resources/read` | Read one resource by URI |
|
`POST .../export` | One JSON snapshot of tools, resources, and prompts |\n| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE .../accounts[/{account}
]` | The server's accounts. See [Server accounts](#server-accounts) |\n| `POST .../oauth/import-tokens` | **Deprecated.** Uploads
to your default account; use `PUT .../accounts/{account}`. See [The deprecated import route](#the-deprecated-import-route) |\n\n**
